headline: You have far more than five senses—scientists count at least 21
universal_truth: There is more information available than we consciously notice
fun_facts: Beyond the famous five, you have proprioception (body position), thermoception (temperature), and nociception (pain)
Your nose can distinguish over 1 trillion different scents—far more than the classic estimate of 10,000
The tongue map showing different taste zones is a myth—all areas taste all flavors
discussion_questions: Which sense do you rely on most? Which do you neglect?
What might you be missing by not paying attention to your lesser-known senses?
How does losing one sense—even temporarily—change your awareness?

hook.title: Welcome
hook.script: You learned you have five senses: sight, sound, smell, taste, touch. But that's not quite right. Scientists now count at least 21 distinct senses—and some say more. Today, we discover the senses you didn't know you had.

options.text: I want to learn something new
options.response: Perfect. Curiosity is the first step to understanding. Let's explore this together.
That curiosity is exactly what we need. Let's dive in and discover something amazing.

cliff.title: The Question
cliff.script: Close your eyes and touch your nose. You did that without looking. How? Not with any of the classic five senses. You used something else—a sense that has a name and works constantly without you noticing.
cliff.prompt: What sense lets you know where your body parts are?

options.response: Exactly. Proprioception is your body's internal GPS—always tracking where everything is.
Touch is involved, but there's a dedicated sense for this...

q1.title: The Hidden Senses
q1.script: Proprioception tells you where your limbs are. Thermoception detects temperature. Nociception signals pain. Equilibrioception keeps you balanced. Chronoception tracks time. Each is as real as sight or sound—just less famous.
q1.prompt: What's your first impression of "The Hidden Senses"?

options.text: This confirms what I already knew
options.response: Great foundation! Now let's build on that knowledge with something you might not expect...
Perfect starting point! This insight will connect to even more surprising facts ahead.

q2.title: Trillion Scents
q2.script: You've heard we can smell 10,000 odors. That number was guessed in 1927. Modern research shows your nose can distinguish over 1 trillion different scent combinations. Your sense of smell is vastly underrated.
q2.prompt: How does this connect to what you already know?

options.response: Exactly. These connections are how knowledge becomes understanding.

options.text: I need to think about this more
options.response: That's a good instinct. Deep understanding takes time. The next fact will help clarify.

q3.title: Tongue Map Myth
q3.script: The tongue map—sweet on the tip, bitter in the back—was debunked decades ago. All areas of your tongue can taste all five flavors: sweet, sour, salty, bitter, and umami. The myth came from a mistranslated 1901 German thesis.
q3.prompt: What surprises you most about this?

options.text: I never thought about it this way
options.response: That shift in perspective is exactly the point. New angles reveal new truths.
That's learning in action. When understanding shifts, you're really getting it.

wisdom.title: Today's Wisdom
wisdom.script: Here's today's wisdom: Your senses deliver far more information than you consciously process. Slowing down to really see, really taste, really feel—this is how we wake up to the richness that's always already there.
wisdom.prompt: What resonates most with you today?

options.response: That central truth will stay with you. Let it guide your thinking.
Application is where knowledge becomes wisdom. That's the real learning.

outro.title: See You Tomorrow
outro.script: That's Day 20—twenty days of learning together! Tomorrow, we'll explore what makes things grow. Until then, try engaging a sense you usually ignore. What do you discover?
outro.prompt: Before you go—what will you take from today?

options.response: Reflection deepens learning. Let these ideas simmer in your mind.
Teaching others is the best way to learn. You've already begun the ripple.

growTrack.title: Sensory Exploration - One Focused Sense
growTrack.learning_objective: Heighten awareness by focusing on an underused sense
growTrack.activity: During one meal today, eat the first few bites with your eyes closed. Focus entirely on taste, texture, temperature, and smell. Notice how shutting off sight amplifies your other senses.
